in_arabic.name: ريم
in_arabic.meaning: ريم تعني الفتاة الجميلة ذات الوجه الحسن
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم ريم مشتق من الفعل ريم الذي يعني التباعد أو الابتعاد، وفي اللغة العربية يعني الفتاة الجميلة ذات الوجه الحسن، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الفرقان الآية ٢٤ {وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا} لا يوجد تفسير مباشر للاسم ريم في القرآن ولكنها تعبر عن الجمال

in_urdu.name: ریما
in_urdu.meaning: ریما کا مطلب خوبصورت چہرے والی لڑکی ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: ریما نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے خوبصورت چہرے والی لڑکی، یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں خوبصورت اور پیاری لڑکی کے معنی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، عربی زبان میں ريم جیسے الفاظ کا استعمال خوبصورتی کی تعریف کے لئے کیا جاتا ہے

in_hindi.name: रीमा
in_hindi.meaning: रीमा का अर्थ है सुंदर चेहरे वाली लड़की
in_hindi.long_meaning: रीमा नाम का अर्थ सुंदरता और प्यार से है, यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत पसंद किया जाता है, इस नाम का चयन अक्सर सुंदर और दयालु स्वभाव की लड़कियों के लिए किया जाता है

in_pashto.name: رېما
in_pashto.meaning: رېما د ښکلې مخ شوې نجلۍ معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: رېما نوم د پښتو کلتور او ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، دا نوم د ښکلې مخ شوې نجلۍ په معنی دی، دا نوم په افغان او پښتني ټولنو کې د یوې ښکلې او مهربانې نجلۍ په توګه کارول کیږي

in_english.name: Reema
in_english.meaning: Reema means beautiful girl or pleasant
in_english.long_meaning: Reema is derived from the Arabic root 'Rim' which means to be distant or remote, but in the context of names, it signifies a beautiful girl or one with a pleasant face, although not directly mentioned in the Quran, the name embodies the qualities of beauty and kindness highly valued in Islamic tradition

data.cultural_impact: The name "Reema" has a gentle and flowing quality to it, which can be seen as a representation of the soft and nurturing nature of Islamic culture. In Arabic cultures, names are often significant and can influence the way people perceive and interact with an individual. A name like Reema suggests a person who is kind, gentle, and caring. In Islamic society, these qualities are highly valued and promoted.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Reema" can be seen as a reminder of the gently flowing waters of Zamzam, the sacred well in Mecca that is believed to have been created by the Prophet Ibrahim and his wife Hajar for their son Ismail. The water from this well is considered to be a source of life and sustenance for millions of pilgrims who visit Mecca every year. In Islamic tradition, the name Reema can be seen as a reflection of the divine mercy and compassion that is embodied in the gentle and flowing waters of Zamzam. It is a reminder of the spiritual nourishment that we receive from Allah, and the importance of being kind, gentle, and compassionate to others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 11, Page 286 The name Reema carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Reema bint Milhan was the wife of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, the powerful Meccan leader. She is known for her role in the early conversion of her husband to Islam before the migration to Medina. According to tradition, she was the one who suggested that the Quran be recited to her husband while he was ill. After hearing the verses, Abu Sufyan is said to have exclaimed, 'By Allah! I know not what I used to worship before but this [Islam] is the truth!'

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz Al-Sahabah, Volume 1, Page 371 The name Reema carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Reema bint Al-Munadhir was an early Muslim woman from the Banu Jumah tribe. She is known for her extraordinary piety and devotion. She used to spend her nights in prayer and fasting, and her days in visiting the sick and taking care of the orphans. She also had a deep influence on her husband, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who later became a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).
